lesson.title: Glacial processes and landforms
lesson.body: At the peak of the last glacial period, around 20,000 years ago, ice covered about two-thirds of the UK. By around 10,000 years ago the ice had retreated, leaving uplands like the Lake District and Snowdonia completely reshaped.

flash.typed: water in cracks freezes, expands and breaks the rock
flash.model: Water seeps into cracks in rock, freezes and expands by about 9%, widening the crack. Repeated cycles shatter the rock.

practice.question: A village population grew from 2,000 to 2,500. What is the percentage increase?
practice.feedback: Right. The increase over the start, times 100.

practice.question: A student measures soil temperature every 10 metres along a 100 m transect. What type of sampling is this?
practice.feedback: Right. A regular interval makes it systematic.

exam.question: Describe the characteristics of a glacial trough.
exam.answer: A glacial trough is U-shaped, with a wide flat floor and steep, almost vertical sides. It is straight because the glacier cut off the interlocking spurs, leaving truncated spurs. Deeper parts can hold ribbon lakes, like Windermere.
exam.well: The U-shape, three features and a named example.
exam.next: Add the misfit stream on the valley floor.

q1.question: Meltwater freezes around jointed bedrock, then the moving ice tears the blocks away. Which process is this?
why: Abrasion is rock fragments in the ice

q2.question: Which landform forms where a tributary glacier could not erode as deeply as the main glacier?
q2.right: Right. The side valley is left hanging above the main one.
